title: Knowledge
takeaway: Knowledge makes you rich in a way no thief can steal.
scene: A short poem in praise of 'ilm', which means knowledge or learning. The poet was a doctor and the father of teachers and students, and he clearly valued education deeply.

original: بندہ علم دے نال انسان بن دا یارو
فیر اوس نوں ملے توقیر یارو
transliteration: Banda ilm de naal insaan banda yaaro
Pher os nu mile tauqeer yaaro
translation: Friends, it's through knowledge that a person becomes truly human;
couplets.story: Learning is what makes us fully human. And once you've learned, people respect you.

original: حق باطل دی ہو پچھان جاندی
transliteration: Haq baatil di ho pachhaan jaandi
translation: You learn to tell truth from falsehood;
without any money, you become rich, friends.
couplets.story: Knowledge helps you tell what's true from what's false. It makes you rich even if you have no money.

original: لتھے کنڈ توں بھار جہالتاں دا
transliteration: Latthe kand ton bhaar jahaalataan da
translation: The weight of ignorance comes off your back;
it brings light to whole nations, friends.
couplets.story: Learning takes the heavy load of ignorance off your shoulders. It brings light to whole countries.

original: جاگ پیندا اے اوہدا ضمیر یارو
چور جہوں ناں احمدؔ چرا سکے
transliteration: Jaag painda ae ohda zameer yaaro
Chor jihnu naa Ahmad chura sake
translation: A person's conscience wakes up, friends.
Ahmad, it's something no thief can steal:
couplets.story: Learning wakes up your conscience. And it's one treasure no thief can ever take from you.

original: علم دولت ہے اوہ جاگیر یارو
transliteration: Ilm daulat hai oh jaageer yaaro
translation: knowledge is that wealth, that estate, friends.
couplets.story: Knowledge is the kind of wealth, the kind of property, that's yours for good.

deeper:
Seeking knowledge is a central value in Islam. The first word revealed in the Qur'an was 'Read!' (96:1), and the Prophet said seeking knowledge is a duty for every Muslim.

The poem says knowledge does two things inside a person. It 'wakes up the conscience', and it lets you 'tell truth from falsehood' (haq and baatil). So learning isn't only for getting a job. It makes you more awake, and an awake person is closer to God.
why: An easy, uplifting poem for students: knowledge is the one treasure no one can take from you.
prompt: What's the most valuable thing you've ever learned, something nobody could take away?
notes: Printed as short lines; grouped into rough couplets here. Line 3 of the third pair is partly shadowed: 'kora mullataan' is read loosely as 'whole nations' (millataan).
